sources.title: Democratizing access to large-scale language models with OPT-175B
sources.evidence: Announcement dated May 3, 2022 explicitly says the smaller baselines are fully released and lists 13 billion among them. Identifies Meta AI and research-oriented noncommercial release.

sources.title: OPT: Open Pre-trained Transformer Language Models, technical report
sources.evidence: Section 2 and Table 1 give the 13B variant 40 decoder Transformer layers, 40 attention heads and width 5120. All variants use ReLU and 2048-token training sequences. Appendix D says the smaller baselines share the noncommercial weight license. The report describes text pretraining and zero/few-shot evaluation, not dedicated reasoning or tool-call features. Reopened October 27, 2026: Table 1 retains the nominal 13B model size; the full report does not define a separate active-parameter count.

sources.title: Meta metaseq: OPT pretrained weights
sources.evidence: Official release table names OPT-13B, gives nominal 13B parameters and downloadable pretrained weight shards. Directs weight use to MODEL_LICENSE.md; current shard paths are later repackagings, not evidence of initial release date. Reopened October 27, 2026: the official table still explicitly lists OPT-13B with 13B parameters, supporting the nominal size independently of an exact tensor count.

sources.title: facebook/opt-13b configuration at e515202d
sources.evidence: Exact checkpoint specifies OPTForCausalLM, 40 layers, hidden and embedding widths 5120, FFN width 20480, 40 heads, vocabulary 50272, 2048 positions, ReLU, float16 and enabled final layer norm. No separate embedding projection is required because embedding and hidden widths match. Reopened the exact revision configuration on October 27, 2026; these dimensions and final-normalization setting are unchanged.

sources.title: facebook/opt-13b checkpoint tensor index at e515202d
sources.evidence: All 644 named entries match the configuration-derived parameter tensors: 16 tensors per layer plus token embeddings, position embeddings and final decoder norm weight/bias. No separate output-head tensor or quantization/buffer entries. Metadata total_size=25,706,946,560 bytes agrees with the derived unique count at two bytes per FP16 element; storage size is only a cross-check.

sources.title: Transformers v4.21.0 OPT implementation
sources.evidence: Defines learned positions with an offset of two rows, biased Q/K/V/output attention projections, biased FFN layers, two affine layer norms per block and a final decoder norm under this configuration. The bias-free language-model output head is tied to token embeddings. v4.21 includes the final norm required by the exact checkpoint, unlike older v4.20 code.

sources.title: Meta OPT baseline training launcher
sources.evidence: OPT baseline launch configuration enables shared decoder input/output embeddings, ReLU and the Transformer language-model architecture, with the chosen variant dimensions.

sources.title: Meta metaseq Transformer decoder implementation
sources.evidence: Official decoder builds sequential Transformer layers, learned position embeddings and a final affine layer norm. With shared input/output embeddings enabled, the output projection references the same token-embedding weight rather than independent learned weights.

sources.title: OPT-175B License Agreement distributed with OPT-13B
sources.evidence: The exact OPT-13B repository distributes Meta's OPT license. Section 1(a) grants use solely for non-commercial research; Section 2(a) excludes commercial/production purposes. The agreement title does not restrict its applicability to only the 175B variant, as confirmed by Meta's smaller-model documentation.

sources.title: facebook/opt-13b hosted model card at e515202d
sources.publisher: Hugging Face team, hosted in Meta facebook repository
sources.evidence: Explicitly identifies itself as authored by the Hugging Face team, pointing to Meta's report for the original card. Describes OPT as a pretrained-only, self-supervised causal language model for text generation and prompted evaluation. Used to check the exact hosted variant, not as sole Meta-authored release evidence.

sources.title: Hugging Face metadata for facebook/opt-13b
sources.evidence: Repository revision e515202d1e7750da62d245fbccb2723b9c1790f5; repository created May 11, 2022. This later hosting date is distinct from Meta's explicit May 3 model release.

sources.title: μ-MoE: Test-Time Pruning as Micro-Grained Mixture-of-Experts
sources.publisher: Toshiaki Koike-Akino, Jing Liu and Ye Wang / Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Table 1 includes OPT-13B and reports 60%, 50% and 40% active weights for compressed variants. Section 2 defines the fraction within a pruned linear weight matrix, and Section 3 says the experiment compresses Transformer linear layers. Original-model perplexities appear beside the model names. Appendix C Table 5 identifies facebook/opt-13b. These percentages are not an absolute active-parameter count for the unchanged checkpoint; they cannot establish 13B active by multiplying a model name or transferring the LLaVA 100% baseline.

sources.title: MoE++: Accelerating Mixture-of-Experts Methods with Zero-Computation Experts
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Table 4 explicitly reports activated/total counts for OPT-1.3B (1.3B/1.3B) and OPT-2.7B (2.7B/2.7B), but does not list OPT-13B. The comparison convention is original research evidence for those exact smaller variants and cannot be transferred to OPT-13B.

sources.title: Prompt-prompted Adaptive Structured Pruning for Efficient LLM Generation
sources.publisher: Harry Dong, Beidi Chen and Yuejie Chi / Carnegie Mellon University
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 after targeted active-count searches. Tables 1 and 2 evaluate OPT 13B and pruned alternatives at 50% feedforward sparsity, without an active-parameter column. The explicit 13B-to-8.8B active-count example in Section 4.2 identifies Llama 2 13B, not OPT 13B. This supplies no absolute active count for the unchanged OPT checkpoint.

name.note: Display-name spacing corresponds to the official OPT-13B checkpoint; this is the base 13B variant.

developer.note: Developed and released by Meta AI; Meta is the catalog developer label.

family.note: OPT family; configuration model_type is opt.

release_date.note: Meta's dated announcement explicitly fully releases the 13B baseline on this day. The May 2 arXiv submission and May 11 Hugging Face repository creation are not substituted for the weight-release date.

open_weights.note: The exact 13B pretrained weights are downloadable under research restrictions. Open weights does not mean an unrestricted open-source license.

license.note: Supported descriptive label for the Meta OPT agreement supplied with this checkpoint; do not use the metaseq/Transformers software license for the weights.

parameters_b.note: Retain the previously reconciled 12,853,473,280 unique parameter elements (12.85347328 decimal billions), which is consistent with Meta's nominal 13B size freshly confirmed in the official release table and technical report on October 27, 2026. The exact checkpoint configuration was reopened and retains the audited dimensions. The prior derivation is L*(4*d*d+2*d*f+9*d+f)+V*d+(P+2)*d+2*d for L=40,d=5120,f=20480,V=50272,P=2048: tied token/output embeddings count once; positional offsets, attention/FFN biases and affine norms are included. That derivation was reconciled to 644 index entries, with FP16 storage only corroborative. No new tensor census or weight download was performed in this pass.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27, 2026 review of Meta's report, release table and exact configuration found no separate active count. Targeted searches for OPT-13B active/activated parameters and active weights led to original comparison papers: μ-MoE reports pruning ratios for linear layers rather than an absolute unchanged-model count; MoE++ explicitly lists only the 1.3B and 2.7B OPT variants; GRIFFIN's absolute 13B active example is Llama 2 13B. Retain null for OPT-13B; neither dense architecture, a pruning percentage nor a sibling model establishes its active count.

architecture.note: Dense decoder-only Transformer: 40 blocks with ordinary multi-head causal self-attention and ReLU feed-forward layers; no expert/router subsystem in this checkpoint implementation or tensor inventory.

context_window.note: Configuration max_position_embeddings and report training sequence length are 2048 tokens. The implementation's two extra positional-table rows are indexing offsets, not an extension to 2050-token context.

modalities.note: Text token input and vocabulary-logit/text continuation output; exact base checkpoint contains no image, audio or video encoders/heads.

reasoning.note: The sources describe a base pretrained causal language model, with no separately documented dedicated reasoning mode or reasoning-training feature. Prompted task performance does not establish such a feature; null does not claim inability to reason.

tool_call.note: The exact checkpoint is documented for text completion; no native tool-call schema, protocol or dedicated tool-use training is specified. External scaffolding or generated text is not evidence of native tool calling.

description.note: The concise baseline description accurately identifies the OPT research checkpoint without unsupported performance claims.

patch.notes: Meta publishes OPT-13B as nominally 13B parameters; the audited configuration and implementation reconcile 12.85347328B unique parameters, counting tied embeddings once. A separate active-parameter count remains unestablished; published pruning ratios concern modified linear layers. Dedicated reasoning and tool-call capabilities are not separately documented. Weights use the OPT non-commercial research license.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit confirms Meta's nominal 13B specification and retains the previously reconciled 12.85347328B unique total. Active parameters remain undisclosed after reopening primary model documents and original comparison papers: μ-MoE supplies pruning percentages, MoE++ omits OPT-13B, and GRIFFIN's absolute 13B active example concerns Llama 2. Explicitly patch the total and null active count, refresh the evidence and public notes, and preserve the other 12 field assessments.
